subScores.label: Team
subScores.rationale: Strong founder-market fit via Zack Eakin's Anduril background in drone manufacturing; technical depth likely high for hardware robotics; but incomplete data on other co-founders and no prior exits documented.

subScores.label: Defensibility
subScores.rationale: No public evidence of proprietary data, workflow lock-in, or network effects; hardware may create switching costs post-deployment but early stage; unclear if differentiation relies on a horizontal platform.

subScores.label: Product
subScores.rationale: One-liner is vague ('Robotics and hardware startup'); likely AI-native physical agents but not confirmed; hardware typically requires non-self-serve onboarding; product articulation weak.

subScores.label: Market & Why-Now
subScores.rationale: No specific vertical or market size hint provided; why-now drivers not articulated; competitive landscape and wedge unknown.

subScores.label: Traction / Freshness
subScores.rationale: Raised $42M Series A per fundedstartupsdaily.com, indicating strong investor confidence and recent capital; however, no disclosed paying customers, active usage metrics, or product launch signals.

scoreRationale: Layup Parts shows strong team pedigree in hardware/robotics and significant fresh capital, but lacks public clarity on product, market focus, defensibility, and commercial traction beyond funding. High execution risk typical of early-stage deep tech hardware.
